mods/aeroengine.pw.toml.aeroengineering.ponder.basic_turbofan_en: Assemble the five-block engine core from intake to exhaust.
The Engine Fan sits at the intake end.
The Compressor is placed directly behind the fan.
The Combustor sits in the middle and burns Aviation Kerosene.
The Turbine is installed behind the combustor.
The Exhaust Cone finishes the basic five-block core.
When all five blocks are ordered and facing correctly, the engine can run.
Fluid systems can deliver Aviation Kerosene.
Shift-right-click the Combustor to configure redstone frequencies and the step size for increasing or decreasing engine power.
Configure the redstone frequency that switches thrust reverser on.
Bind an Engine Gearbox to the Combustor, then place it within the surrounding 3x3x3 area. It outputs kinetic stress capacity while the Combustor is started.
Without casing, the engine spins and produces thrust.
Engine Casing can encase fluid pipes near the engine.
Engine Casing and its three copycat variants can surround the core and greatly increase thrust.
An Exhaust Nozzle ring or any of its three copycat variants gives extra thrust.
When the Thrust Reverser is switched on, it produces small reverse thrust.
mods/aeroengine.pw.toml.aeroengineering.ponder.high_bypass_turbo: Build a high-bypass turbofan by replacing the intake Engine Fan with a Large Engine Fan.
The Large Engine Fan sits at the intake end and provides the bypass airflow.
The Compressor still sits directly behind the fan.
The Combustor burns Aviation Kerosene in the engine core.
The rest of the five-block turbofan core remains Compressor, Combustor, Turbine, and Exhaust Cone.
Fuel delivery works the same as a normal turbofan.
Configure the Combustor frequencies and power step just like the basic turbofan.
Bind an Engine Gearbox to the Combustor, then place it within the surrounding 3x3x3 area. It outputs kinetic stress capacity while the Combustor is started.
Without casing, the high-bypass turbofan already spins and produces thrust.
The Large Engine Fan does not need a surrounding casing ring to keep the engine casing complete.
Casing starts behind the Large Engine Fan, around the Compressor and hot core, and still increases thrust.
An Exhaust Nozzle ring behind the engine adds more thrust.
High-bypass turbofans can use the Exhaust Cone thrust reverser frequency.
When reverse thrust is active, the airflow points forward and produces small reverse thrust.
Right-click the Large Engine Fan, then scroll its value box to change propeller size.
Scrolling the value up makes the Large Engine Fan visibly larger.
mods/aeroengine.pw.toml.aeroengineering.ponder.afterburning_turb: Assemble the afterburning engine core from intake to exhaust.
The Engine Fan sits at the intake end.
The Compressor is placed directly behind the fan.
The Combustor sits in the middle and burns Aviation Kerosene.
The Turbine is installed behind the combustor.
Use an Afterburner instead of the Exhaust Cone to build an afterburning turbofan core.
This core can run normally, then switch to afterburning when signalled.
Fluid systems can deliver Aviation Kerosene.
Configure the redstone frequencies and power step used to raise or lower engine power.
Bind an Engine Gearbox to the Combustor, then place it within the surrounding 3x3x3 area. It outputs kinetic stress capacity while the Combustor is started.
Configure the redstone frequency that switches the Afterburner on.
Without casing, the engine spins and produces thrust.
Engine Casing can encase fluid pipes near the engine.
Engine Casing and its three copycat variants can surround the core and greatly increase thrust.
Afterburning engines can use a matching Exhaust Nozzle ring or any of its three copycat variants.
When the Afterburner is switched on, it produces enormous thrust and burns Aviation Kerosene much faster.
mods/aeroengine.pw.toml.aeroengineering.ponder.variable_airflow_: Variable Airflow Afterburning Turbofan Engine Operation
Assemble the variable airflow afterburning engine core from intake to exhaust.
The Engine Fan sits at the intake end.
The Compressor is placed directly behind the fan.
The Combustor sits in the middle and burns Aviation Kerosene.
The Turbine is installed behind the combustor.
Use a Variable Airflow Afterburner behind the turbine to enable adjustable exhaust flow.
Attach a Variable Airflow Nozzle directly behind it; this replaces the normal nozzle ring.
The nozzle reads the Combustor's signal and animates its blades to match engine power.
Fluid systems can deliver Aviation Kerosene.
Configure the redstone frequencies and power step used to raise or lower engine power.
Bind an Engine Gearbox to the Combustor, then place it within the surrounding 3x3x3 area. It outputs kinetic stress capacity while the Combustor is started.
Configure the afterburner frequency separately; when it is active, the nozzle opens fully.
Without casing, the engine spins and produces thrust.
Engine Casing can encase fluid pipes near the engine.
Engine Casing and its three copycat variants can surround the core and greatly increase thrust.
A complete Variable Airflow Nozzle changes its opening with the Combustor's current signal strength.
Signal strength 3 keeps the nozzle wide and the exhaust broad for low power.
Signal strength 9 narrows the nozzle and strengthens the exhaust stream.
Signal strength 15 closes the nozzle furthest and produces the strongest normal airflow.
When afterburning is switched on, the afterburner beam takes over and the nozzle opens for maximum flow.
mods/aeroengine.pw.toml.aeroengineering.ponder.vector_afterburni: Assemble the vectoring afterburning engine core from intake to exhaust.
The Engine Fan sits at the intake end.
The Compressor is placed directly behind the fan.
The Combustor sits in the middle and burns Aviation Kerosene.
The Turbine is installed behind the combustor.
Install the vectoring afterburner mechanism behind the turbine to control thrust direction and afterburning.
The core can run normally while the vectoring mechanism controls exhaust direction and afterburning.
Fluid systems can deliver Aviation Kerosene.
Configure the redstone frequencies and power step used to start the engine and change its power.
Bind an Engine Gearbox to the Combustor, then place it within the surrounding 3x3x3 area. It outputs kinetic stress capacity while the Combustor is started.
Configure four vector direction frequencies and an independent afterburner frequency.
Without casing, the engine spins and produces thrust.
Engine Casing can encase fluid pipes near the engine.
Engine Casing and its three copycat variants can surround the core and greatly increase thrust.
The Exhaust Nozzle and its three copycat variants can form the tilting ring, and exhaust particles follow it.
Afterburning produces enormous thrust and consumes fuel faster while the exhaust follows the tilted nozzle.
mods/aeroengine.pw.toml.aeroengineering.ponder.airborne_radar.te: The Airborne Radar scans nearby physicalized Sable structures.
The Radar needs external kinetic stress. Connect power to its shaft axis before it can scan.
It consumes kinetic stress; higher absolute rotation speed gives a longer scan range.
Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to open the fire-control frequency menu.
The menu has three redstone-link frequency pairs: Switch, Confirm, and Launch.
Switch Target cycles the tracked target among valid fire-control contacts while no target is confirmed.
Confirm / Cancel locks the tracked target. Trigger it again to cancel the confirmed lock.
Launch Missile fires one ready bound launcher at the confirmed target, then clears the lock.
Fire-control contacts must be inside radar range and inside the forward aim cone.
A nearby Velocity Sensor supplies the preferred forward direction; otherwise the radar uses structure motion, then block facing.
Right-click the Radar with a single Missile Assembly Station item to reserve and bind a launcher slot. A Radar can bind up to 8 stations.
Place the bound station. It registers with the Radar and can launch ready assembled missiles.
Wrench a bound station to highlight the Radar it belongs to.
The bound Radar is highlighted so you can find and manage the launcher connection.
Open the Radar menu and press Reset Launchers to clear every reserved or placed launcher binding.
mods/aeroengine.pw.toml.aeroengineering.ponder.hud_display.text_: Place the HUD Display directly above the Simulated Linked Typewriter, in front of a Create Seat.
Sneak-right-click the Display with a configured Pilot Helmet to copy the helmet HUD data onto the screen.
The Display renders the same enabled HUD instruments and monitor entries as the helmet.
Bind engine and weapon blocks, such as a Combustor and Missile Assembly Station, to show power state and launcher loadout.
Bind a Navigation Table, Velocity Sensor, Gimbal Sensor, and Altitude Sensor for navigation and flight instruments.
When the copied helmet data includes an Airborne Radar, fire-control contacts appear on the HUD Display.
Nearby physicalized structures become radar contacts behind the pilot's forward view.
As contacts move, the HUD Display updates their relative positions.
Trigger the Switch Target frequency to move the tracked target marker between contacts.
Trigger Confirm / Cancel to turn the tracked marker into a confirmed fire-control lock.
Trigger Launch Missile after confirming a target; the HUD Display clears or changes the lock as fire control updates.
If no copied helmet data is present, the screen shows the empty HUD message instead.
mods/aeroengine.pw.toml.aeroengineering.ponder.missile_assembly_: Right-click the Radar with a Missile Assembly Station item to bind a launcher slot before placing it.
Build a multi-block missile directly below the station. Light gray concrete is enough for this example.
Use Super Glue to frame the missile body so the station can assemble the whole glued structure.
Right-click the station with a Missile Thruster. The thruster mounts below the station and carries the assembled missile.
The Lever is placed one block above the Assembly Station.
Power the station with redstone, such as a Lever, to assemble the glued missile body onto the thruster.
After assembly, the station is loaded and the bound Radar can launch it when fire control sends Launch Missile.
mods/aeroengine.pw.toml.aeroengineering.ponder.pilot_helmet.head: Binding and configuring the Pilot Helmet
mods/aeroengine.pw.toml.aeroengineering.ponder.pilot_helmet.text: Targets must be inside the same physicalized Sable structure.
Hold the Pilot Helmet and sneak-right-click a readable block to bind it.
Repeat this on other blocks in that structure. Sneak-right-click a bound block again to remove it.
Equip the helmet, then press the HUD manager key (H by default).
Select a target to rename it, hide it, or choose which information entries it displays.
Dynamic HUD instruments use Altitude, Velocity, Gimbal, and Navigation targets.
Engine blocks still use normal information panels; they do not create flight instruments.
The Altitude Sensor supplies the altitude tape on the dynamic HUD.
The Velocity Sensor supplies speed and heading. Reverse its positive direction when the HUD direction does not match the physical structure.
The Gimbal Sensor supplies pitch and roll. Swap the pitch and roll axes when their HUD directions do not match the physical structure.
The Navigation Table still accepts its normal targets, including compasses, recovery compasses, maps, and redstone magnets.
It also accepts a configured Coordinate Form as a waypoint target.
A Coordinate Form adds a target approach heading to the HUD. Bind a Velocity Sensor as well so the HUD can compare the structure's heading with the approach direction.
The HUD manager can toggle dynamic instruments, resize them, and apply the direction corrections for each matching sensor.
A helmet supports up to 12 targets, all belonging to one physical structure.

mods/create-propulsion-simulated.pw.toml.createpropulsion.ponder.shared.thruster_: Thrusters accept configured fuels through connected pipes.
Invalid fluids do not power the thruster.
Use valid thruster fuels in the input line.
Now apply redstone power so the thruster actually produces thrust.
2x2 multiblocks only accept fluid from the rear intake side.
A 2x2x2 multiblock is built from 8 normal thrusters.
First line (no clutch) is invalid here: it is not pumping into the rear intake.
Because this line does not feed the rear tanks, the thruster does nothing.
You can only feed from the rear side for multiblocks.
Remove the invalid top line and feed from the rear side instead.
You can only feed from the rear side for multiblocks.
With the valid rear-fed line, insert proper thruster fuel.
Finally apply redstone to the thruster: now it actually runs.
3x3 multiblocks follow the same rear-intake-only rule.
A 3x3x3 multiblock is built from 27 normal thrusters.
You can only feed from the rear side for multiblocks.
Feed the back layer input manifold for full operation.
Insert valid thruster fuel into the rear-fed manifold.
Apply redstone to the thruster and the whole multiblock works.
mods/create-propulsion-simulated.pw.toml.createpropulsion.ponder.shared.vector_th: Vector Thruster uses Forge energy to produce thrust.
Forge energy is stored in the thruster's internal energy storage.
Currently %s FE is able to be stored in the thruster's internal storage.
Generators can power from below, this can be anything that uses forge energy system.
Vector Thrusters can rotate in all directions, this is controlled by redstone signals directly embedded into the thruster itself.
A redstone power can be anything from 0-15, this will increase the distance of rotation from the base.
Each side except front and back has a redstone signal place, that direction is where it will be rotated towards when that signal is powered.
Powering a thruster is easy, any external signal to the thruster will be the power, this can range from 0-15, and will use power accordingly.
Creative Vector Thrusters produce configurable thrust without fuel or Forge energy.
Set the creative thrust amount from the value box on the bottom of the thruster.
Creative Vector Thrusters still use redstone power as their throttle, from 0-15.
Liquid Vector Thrusters vector their thrust like normal vector thrusters, but run on pumped liquid fuel.
Pump valid thruster fuel into the liquid vector thruster through the pipe below.
Once fuel is pumped in, the internal tank can feed the thruster while it is powered.
Apply redstone power to throttle the liquid vector thruster, from 0-15.

mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_crafting/: Using the Basin Foundry Lid
Basin Foundry Lids are used to melt down metals for cannon casting.
They must be heated to process melting recipes.
Boring Holes in Cast Cannons
Cannon Drills are used to bore out cast cannons.
In addition to rotational force, they require water to operate, and consume more as they speed up.
The speed of the drill must match the speed of the lathe to do work.
Bored cannon blocks drop scrap items.
Building Built-Up Cannons
Cannon Builders are used to put together the layers of built-up cannons.
Pulse the Cannon Builder with power to toggle its attachment state.
When grabbing layers from built-up blocks, the outermost layer will always be grabbed
Cannon Casting
Cannon Casts are the first block recipe for cannon blocks.
It is possible to automate the removal of finished casts.
Smaller cannons such as autocannons shed the casting sand automatically.
Use a cannon mould to build a cast layer.
Deployers can also interact with cannon casts.
Fill the cast with molten metal to start the casting process.
Cannon casts output a signal that can be read by comparators.
They output a signal from 0 to 14 measuring how full the cast is, and 15 when the cast is finished.
After being completely filled up, the cannon cast takes some time to solidify.
The time it takes for the casting process to finish depends on the size of the cast.
The finished cannon cast can be removed by breaking or interacting with it.
Using the Cannon Welder
Cannon blocks placed in survival will not connect to other cannon blocks.
The Cannon Welder can quickly connect two cannon blocks at a time.
Right-click two adjacent cannon blocks to weld them together.
The cannon blocks must align, connect, have the same material, and have the same cannon type.
Invalid
By default, the Cannon Welder cannot weld some cannon materials and/or types together.
The Cannon Welder can weld different types of cannon.
Welding cannon blocks together can weaken certain types of cannon.
It is recommended to craft and move cannon pieces in their entirety instead.
Finishing Built-Up Cannons
Blasting built-up cannon layers turns them into built-up cannon blocks.
The process works similar to bulk blasting of items, using a fan blowing into a lava block to produce a heating current.
A built-up cannon block must have all the correct layers to be transformed.
It takes a while for the cannon layers to transform into cannon blocks.
Incomplete Cannon Blocks
Some bored cannon blocks need additional items to be completed.
These are usually cannon breech blocks.
Use the listed items on the block to complete it.
Deployers can also complete incomplete cannon blocks.
Creating a Quick-Firing Breech
Use a Quick-Firing Mechanism to convert a Sliding Breech into a Quick-Firing Breech.
Deployers can also be used to create Quick-Firing Breeches.
Wrench a Quick-Firing Breech to revert it back to a Sliding Breech.
Moving Cannons Around
By default, most cast cannons will turn into scrap when broken without a Silk Touch pickaxe.
Create's contraptions can be used in varying ways to move cannons.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_kinetics/: Mechanical Arms can be used to reload the Quick-Firing Breech.
Right-click the Cannon Mount to set the arm's output.
The Quick-Firing Breech must be closed in order for the arm to operate.
The arm will not load the big cannon if the breech is open.
Once the cannon fires, the arm will automatically extract empty cartridges when provided a deposit area.
Deposit areas should have an empty Big Cartridge filter to avoid item mismanagement.
The Quick-Firing Breech allows fast reloading of assembled big cannons.
The Quick-Firing Breech can be opened and closed by right clicking the side of the breech.
First, load the projectile by right clicking the open side of the breech.
Then load the propellant and close the breech.
Big Cartridges are recommended for faster reloading.
The big cannon can then be fired.
Remaining munitions such as spent Big Cartridge cases will be automatically ejected.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_loader/ba: Loading Big Cannons with base Create contraptions
Mechanical Pistons, Gantries, and Rope Pulleys can also load big cannons.
Munition blocks can be pulled out of big cannons depending on the connectivity of certain blocks.
Unlike the Cannon Loader, other blocks can still be attached to the contraption.
This does not affect cannon loading in any way, although only aligned munition blocks can be inserted into big cannons.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_loader/ha: Handloading tools are convenient for loading big cannons.
Munitions can also be inserted directly into assembled big cannons.
Handloading tools can also interact with assembled big cannons.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_loader/lo: Cannon Loaders work like Mechanical Pistons, using Piston Extension Poles to extend their range.
They must be outfitted with a head to be useful, such as a Ram Head or a Worm Head.
Under normal circumstances, the Ram Head should be used.
However, the Worm Head can be attached if the cannon needs to be unjammed.
Before reloading a cannon, it must be disassembled.
When loading a cannon, the loader mechanism, munitions, and cannon must all be in line on the same axis.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_mount/ass: Big cannons need to be placed on cannon mounts to be assembled.
To assemble a cannon, power the hammer face with a redstone signal.
Power the Cannon Mount to aim the cannon up and down...
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_mount/cus: Autocannons can be customized in a few ways, both cosmetic and functional.
Wrenching the end of an autocannon will change the type of barrel end.
Recoil Springs make the barrel push back when firing.
Wrenching the autocannon breech will add handles.
Autocannons with handles are controlled by the player instead of by kinetics.
You can place a seat on the handle breech.
Wrenching the autocannon breech again will remove handles.
Any placed seats will be returned to the player or popped off.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_mount/fir: After loading, assembling, and aiming the cannon, big cannons are ready to fire.
Power the lit cannon face on the cannon mount to fire the mounted cannon.
To disassemble the cannon to prepare it for the next shot, unpower the hammer face.
The cannon instantly snaps back to the position it was assembled at when disassembled.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_mount/scr: Screw Breeches are strong breech blocks that do not suffer strength penalties unlike Sliding Breeches.
Use rotational force to unlock screw breeches.
Once the screw breech is fully unlocked, use kinetic contraptions to move it out of the way for loading.
Once loading is finished, close the screw breech to close the cannon.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_mount/sli: Sliding Breeches offer a quick way to load cannons from the breech, at the cost of cannon strength.
Use rotational force to open up sliding breeches.
Once the sliding breech is fully opened, cannon munitions can be loaded through the breech.
The sliding breech must be not obstructed by munitions or loader contraptions for it to close.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_mount/ups: Cannon Mounts can be rotated to face downwards by clicking their sides with a wrench.
Cannon Mounts can also be placed upside-down on the bottom of blocks.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.cannon_mount/usi: Autocannons fire at a fast rate.
They take in item munitions as input.
Spent ammunition is ejected from the breech.
Power the firing face on the Cannon Mount to make the autocannon shoot.
Increasing the power on the firing face increases the fire rate of the autocannon.
Cannon Mount Extensions provide extra interface areas for blocks.
They extend the mount they point into, as indicated by the arrow on their sides.
Fixed Cannon Mounts can be used for aiming cannons at the same spot.
They do not use kinetic input and must be manually set using the side interfaces.
Interfacing with a Fixed Cannon Mount is similar to a regular Cannon Mount, with the same control faces.
The Fixed Cannon Mount cannot be extended.
Use a wrench to rotate the Fixed Cannon Mount.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.munitions/adding: Adding tracers to big cannon projectiles
In addition to autocannon munitions, tracers can also be added to big cannon projectiles.
Unlike fuzing, tracer tips can be applied to any side of the projectile block.
Right-click the projectile with an empty hand to remove any tracers present.
As with fuzing, tracer application can be automated with Deployers.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.munitions/automa: Automating loading the Autocannon Ammo Container
Mechanical Arms can load assembled autocannons with Autocannon Ammo Containers.
Set a Cannon Mount with an autocannon as one of the Mechanical Arm's deposits.
You can dispose of empty containers by setting a deposit filter slot to an empty container.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.munitions/cannon: When loading a cannon, care must be taken to ensure that cannon loads are safe and effective.
...such as not loading enough Powder Charges...
...allowing a fired projectile to collide with another object in the barrel...
...can cause catastrophic failure and pose a major threat to the surrounding environment.
A cannon's material has two main factors that can cause the cannon to fail; its minimum projectile velocity per barrel and its strength.
The minimum projectile velocity per barrel determines how much power a projectile should have to not get stuck in a cannon.
For example, the default minimum projectile velocity of cast iron is equivalent to 1 Powder Charge for every barrel.
The barrel that the loaded projectile is in is also counted towards the barrels travelled.
The strength of a cannon determines the maximum amount of Powder Charges that can be loaded, after which the cannon has a chance to burst when firing.
For example, cast iron is strong enough to safely handle 2 Powder Charges.
The strength of a cannon can be affected by its breech.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.munitions/fillin: Autocannon Ammo Containers can be filled in-menu.
You can also configure tracer spacing in the menu.
Different ammo types have different capacities.
The container can also be filled with deployers.
Ammo with tracers will go in the tracer slot, otherwise it will go in the main slot.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.munitions/fuzing: Fuzes can be attached to certain projectiles to detonate them under certain conditions.
Right-click the projectile head with an empty hand to remove any fuzes present. Some shells are fuzed on the base instead.
Fuzing projectiles can be automated with Deployers.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.munitions/using_: Autocannon Ammo Containers are a convenient way to store autocannon ammo and to load autocannons.
Right-click a container on an Autocannon Breech to load it.
To remove a container, right-click the breech with an empty hand.
You can also swap out the container by right-clicking the breech with another container.
You can also load an assembled autocannon with a container.
However, you can only remove a present container on an assembled autocannon if it is empty, or by swapping or shift right-clicking it.
mods/create-big-cannons.pw.toml.createbigcannons.ponder.munitions/wet_am: Protecting Munitions with Waterlogging, and its Side Effects
Propellant blocks, as well as projectiles, are vulnerable to exploding from fire and other explosions.
Munition blocks can be protected from fire and explosions by waterlogging them.
However, waterlogging causes propellant blocks to become damp.
Damp propellant is weaker and also fails to ignite if it is placed as the first propellant block in a big cannon.
To fix this, damp propellant must be left to dry, and cannot be dried in a furnace like wet sponges.
However, propellant placed in hot places like the Nether will instantly dry, similar to wet sponges.

mods/escalated.pw.toml.escalated.ponder.tag.walkways.descriptio: How to build walkways and escalators to move around efficiently
mods/escalated.pw.toml.escalated.ponder.walkways/adding_shafts_: Adding more Shafts to Walkways and Escalators
Additional shafts can be added to walkways for more power supply.
To add a shaft, Right-Click a middle walkway block with a Shaft item.
Once added, the walkway block side can be wrenched to block off rotational input from that side.
This also applies to walkway terminals.
To remove the shaft, wrench the block while Sneaking.
Shafts cannot be applied to escalators.
mods/escalated.pw.toml.escalated.ponder.walkways/creating_walkw: Right-Click two shafts with a walkway steps item to create a walkway.
Accidental selections can be cancelled with Right-Click while Sneaking.
Due to the escalator structure, the shafts are not aligned on a perfect diagonal.
The horizontal distance between the shafts is 3 blocks greater than the vertical distance.
mods/escalated.pw.toml.escalated.ponder.walkways/customizing_wa: Customizing Walkways and Escalators with Dyes and Handrails
Walkway and escalator steps can be dyed by Right-Clicking them with a dye item.
To remove the dye, Right-Click the walkway with a water item.
Handrails can be added to the walkway by Right-Clicking the walkway with a belt item.
This will only work if there is space above the walkway.
The handrails can also be dyed and cleaned just like the walkway.
Finally, the handrails can also be made into glass by Right-Clicking them with a glass block.
mods/escalated.pw.toml.escalated.ponder.walkways/widening_walkw: Walkways can be widened by connecting a walkway with an adjacent shaft.
The widening also widens handrails on top.
However, if the handrail is obstructed by something, the handrail will break.

mods/create-steam-n-rails-1.21.1.pw.toml.railways.ponder.train_semaphore.text_1: Semaphores are placed on poles above Train Signals
